To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rats show diurnal variation in the performance (shocks avoided) of a free-opernt avoidance task.

the efficacy of avoidance behavior in rats is a function of the time of day that testing occurs, and that this diurnal variation in efficacy is not due to a change in general activity levels of the animals.
the performance of free-operant avoidance behavior in rats is best in the middle part of the dark phase and worst in the late part of the light phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the analysis of the relationship between the environment and the behavior of the organism.
the effects of the circadian system on the acquisition and performance of avoidance behavior.
the development of a behavioral test for the detection and measurement of neuroleptic-induced catalepsy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present experiment has demonstrated the existence of a diurnal periodicity in the avoidance performance of rats, and that this periodicity should be taken into consideration in the design of experiments involving conditioned behaviors.
the present results suggest the need for more research on diurnal variation of conditioned behaviors.

there was a daily periodicity in the avoidance behavior of the rats, and that the periodicity was not due to general activity levels, or to the periodicity of food intake, or to the circadian rhythm of the rats, or to the time at which the rats were handled for the behavioral tests.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the daily rhythm in performance was a result of the circadian timing system, and that this system was entrained to the 24-h. light/dark cycle.
the performance of free-operant avoidance by rats is not constant throughout the 24-h day.
a diurnal variation in performance was detected in this experiment, that it was not related to general activity levels, and that it was not a consequence of the particular avoidance task employed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time of day when an experiment is conducted may have an impact on the results, and that it should be controlled for in experimental design.
the time of day when an experiment is performed can have a significant influence on the results.
diurnal variation in performance of conditioned behaviors should be considered when designing and conducting experiments.
